name: equal_effort
description: CALIBRATED AND RUN. Isolates evaluation quality from search volume by giving DeepSetsBotExp the extra wall clock it needs to evaluate about as many positions per turn as the stock-speed baseline, instead of the same wall clock. The answer to 'is the network better, or is the heuristic agent just searching more?' is this matchup's win rate. SOT_TIME_SCALE=9.0, timeout 91; achieved 43,139 vs 49,131 evaluations per turn over 400 games, i.e. DeepSetsBotExp at 0.88 of the baseline's effort. Read with equal_effort_baseline_slowed.json, which asks the same question from the other direction.
_why_alpha0_is_zero: SOT_ALPHA0=0 on both the matchup and the calibration block, and it is load-bearing. The question here is about the NETWORK as an evaluator, so the agent measured must be the network-only one, and the calibration must be run on the same agent that is benchmarked -- calibrating at 0.7 and running at 0.0 would match the wrong agent's throughput. At alpha0=0 the pure-network short circuit in Evaluate() fires on every leaf and one counted evaluation is exactly one ONNX forward pass. NOTE this is a definitional argument, not a throughput one: the blend also runs the heuristic inside the same counted evaluation, but that costs only ~1.6% of throughput (paired over 6 seeds), not the factor of 1.8 an earlier version of this note claimed. See experiments/README.md, 'Counting evaluations'.
_calibration: Calibration, DeepSetsBotExp vs SakkirinaScaled, SOT_ALPHA0=0, both sides at scale 1.0:
n = 60 games, ratio of means r = 7.08 (roughly 6.4 to 7.8).
That r is what both equal-effort configs are derived from -- one calibration, two
ACHIEVED, over the 400-game runs (these are the numbers to quote, not r):
DeepSetsBotExp 43,139 vs  SakkirinaScaled 49,131 evals/turn -- DeepSetsBotExp at
0.88 of the baseline's effort, i.e. slightly LESS, not matched.
Why 9.0 and not r = 7.08: evaluations per turn is only approximately linear in the time
budget -- tree reuse and the rule-based fast paths do not scale with the clock -- and a
pilot at 7.08 undershot. 9.0 was chosen empirically from that pilot, not derived.
Both directions landed with DeepSetsBotExp doing slightly less work than the baseline
(0.97x and 0.88x), so in both the residual mismatch runs AGAINST the DeepSets agent. That
is the conservative direction for the claim: a win under these conditions is not explained
by the DeepSets side having been handed more search.
_reproducing_this: To re-derive the scale on different hardware (the ratio is hardware-dependent):
Runs the calibration block below and prints r as a SUGGESTED SOT_TIME_SCALE.
2. Put it in matchups[0].env.SOT_TIME_SCALE, and set matchups[0].timeout to
ceil(9.8 * scale) + 2 -- the engine clock must accommodate the bot's enlarged
per-turn cap, or every turn ends as a TURN_TIMEOUT. At 9.0 that is 91.
3. Re-run --calibrate with those values and check the two evals/turn figures against
each other. Expect to adjust upward, as above: r undershoots.
The harness refuses any matchup whose timeout or env is left as the string TBD, so a
half-filled config cannot quietly run at SOT_TIME_SCALE=1.0 and be labelled
COST: at scale 9.0 the bot-side per-turn cap is 88.2s. Submit with an explicit
--time=00:45:00; slurm_experiment.sh's 00:30:00 default would kill every task.
Budget roughly 120 core-hours for the 400 games. The baseline-slowed direction costs
a normal row and answers the same question -- run that one first.

matchups.label: equal_effort
matchups.note: The baseline stays at 1.0 (stock SakkirinaSolo timing) on purpose -- it is the fixed point the treatment is matched TO. Only DeepSetsBotExp's clock moves. SOT_ALPHA0=0 makes this the pure-network agent (behaviourally DeepSetsBot); see _why_alpha0_is_zero above. SOT_TIME_SCALE=9.0 gives it an 88.2s bot-side per-turn cap, hence timeout 91.

matchups.label: calibrate_stock_speed
matchups.note: SakkirinaScaled rather than SakkirinaSolo because stock SakkirinaSolo emits no throughput telemetry at all, and at SOT_BASELINE_TIME_SCALE=1.0 the two are timing-identical. This is how the stock baseline's evaluations per turn gets measured. SOT_ALPHA0=0 must match the matchup it is calibrating FOR -- calibrating at 0.7 and running at 0.0 would match the wrong agent's throughput.
